memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in obedience to him, to love him, to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and to observe the Lord's commands and decrees that I am giving you today for your own good? - Deut 10:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses gathers the whole of Israel's calling into one beautiful summary: "What does the Lord your God ask of you?" The answer is to fear Him, walk in His ways, love Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul. Notice how relational this is. God is not asking merely for external rule-keeping but for a whole-hearted relationship — reverence, love, obedience, and service flowing together from a devoted heart. And it is all "for your own good."

That last phrase is worth pausing on. God's commands are not a heavy burden designed to make life miserable. They are given "for your own good." A loving Father asks of His children what will bless them, not harm them. When we walk in God's ways, we are walking the path that leads to true flourishing. His requirements flow from His love and aim at our good.

We should be careful not to hear this summary as a checklist we must complete to earn God's favor — that would slip into legalism. Rather, it describes the shape of a life lived in loving response to the God who has already redeemed us. And of course, none of us fulfills this perfectly. That is why we need Jesus, who loved and served the Father flawlessly in our place, and who now pours His Spirit into us so that we can begin to love and serve God from the heart (Rom 5:5). What God asks, He also enables. Ask Him today to grow in you a heart that fears, loves, and serves Him gladly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I see God's commands as a burden or as being "for my own good"?
- Is my relationship with God whole-hearted, or merely external rule-keeping?
- How does Jesus enable me to love and serve God from the heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that what You ask of me is for my own good and flows from Your love. Grow in me a heart that fears You, loves You, and serves You wholeheartedly. Where I fall short, thank You for Jesus who loved You perfectly for me. Amen.
